newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures erased their losses on Monday to finish slightly firmer in thin volume ahead of release of the U.S. consumer price index on Tuesday.
Dealers said that the cash and futures market held up well in the face of U.S. Treasuries' dull performance on Monday.
"We were seeing selling of shorter dated bonds and investors going longer in the curve which is a robust sign," said one analyst.
But mainly the mood was one of wait-and-see ahead of the U.S. consumer price figures, expected to be a key pointer to whether the U.S. Federal Reserve tightens rates further.
The 10-year bond future ended four basis points higher at 128.26 after having traded in a narrow range from 128.04 to 128.38 during the day.
Analysts believe after last Friday's bad surprise from U.S. producer price figures that the market is reasonably well prepared for any bad news from the U.S. consumer prices.

"The U.S. market looks relatively well braced for some bad news. There has been a big correction already through to the two year part of the curve which may prove more aggressive than necessary," said an analyst.
The announcement of stronger-than-expected U.S. producer prices on Friday sent the U.S. debt market tumbling.

"We do not believe France would escape a shakeout in the U.S. market completely," said one analyst. But he said he believed the European market, particularly the French, could hold up better as "we are at a different point in our economic cycle and not in danger of overheating".

"If the U.S. market drops, the French market will drop too, but we expect relatively less than other European markets," said another analyst, citing strong French institutional flows into domestic bonds.
The franc was steady at 3.3644 per mark against 3.3645 on Friday while June PIBOR was unchanged at 96.67 in just 4,975 contracts traded.
